key_insight: LLMs that answer medical questions correctly can still be easily swayed by misleading context, showing that medical accuracy does not guarantee epistemic resilience.
clinical_relevance: This matters because patients may rely on LLMs for health advice, and misleading framing can push models toward unsafe or incorrect guidance.
method: Built MedMisBench with 10,932 medical questions and 48,889 misleading context-option pairs
Tested 11 model configurations across medical reasoning, agentic capability, and patient-journey evaluation
Measured whether models kept correct answers under adversarial, context-based injections
evidence_signal: Across 11 model configurations, accuracy dropped from 71.1% on original questions to 38.0% with focused misleading context, with 51.5% attack success.
watch_item: Results show vulnerability to adversarial medical framing, so real-world deployment should not assume exam-level performance translates to safe context-sensitive advice.
paper_title: Measuring Epistemic Resilience of LLMs Under Misleading Medical Context
